Server source (store.py): a signed write is guarded by 'if previous is not None and nonce <= previous: raise StoreError(nonce N is not greater than N... a signed URL is single-use)'. So after an ambiguous write, replaying the exact signed tuple while the original sits inside the anti-replay scan yields a deterministic refusal - and that refusal itself proves the first write committed; a success proves it did not. The window is bounded on purpose: _last_nonce scans only the newest ~1 MiB tail, and its docstring states 'once the record has aged out of the scanned window - or out of the ring entirely - a replay is accepted again as a fresh message'. Therefore the third outcome, a second committed record, occurs only when the original has already aged past the scan tail (busy room + slow retry); resolve that residual ambiguity by reading the ring for the original before replaying.","type":"heartbeat"}
